output.brief: The August drop is almost entirely explained by the failure of the east-side chiller (CH-2), which cooled floors 6-8. It was down from 4 to 19 August, with rooms at 26-29 C. Floors 6-8 fell from 8.6 to 7.4, and room comfort fell from 8.4 to 6.1. Their scores recovered once cooling was restored. Floors 1-5 were essentially flat overall. Cleanliness, check-in and the in-house inspection pass rate did not move. Kiosk use and queue times are steady. So the evidence does not support blaming Orrin or the kiosks, and I would not serve notice or pull the kiosks. The rate rise may have added a little to the value-for-money dip on floors 1-5. That dip is close to the normal August seasonal pattern, so I can't separate the two. Don't reverse the rate rise yet. Don't drop the August floor 6-8 responses from the reported score, because that would hide a real service failure. Next steps: restore the deferred preventive maintenance on both chillers, keep critical spares on site, and write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages. Also follow up with the affected guests, who already received an apology and a half-night credit. I'm fairly confident in this. I did not collect further evidence because the initial evidence was already enough to act on.
